text: A set L is decidable (recursive) rather than merely semi-decidable (recursively enumerable) exactly when:
choices: L is the domain of some partial computable function
both L and its complement L̄ are semi-decidable
L is recognized by a Turing machine that may run forever on non-members
explanation: The key theorem: L is decidable iff both L and its complement are semi-decidable. Options B and D describe only semi-decidability (r.e.), where the machine may diverge on non-members; option A is irrelevant to decidability. A decider must always halt with the correct verdict, which is exactly what having both L and L̄ r.e. provides.
